title: Interval operator Every vs At; calendar At is a day-and-month picker
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in, on the build under test, as an Owner/Admin or as a user with "Settings Service" enabled.
  2. In the left sidebar under Settings, open the "Maintenance" entry beneath "Inspection Templates" (if the build shows "Maintenance schedules" instead, use that entry and record the label). Schedules are shared by the whole organization, whichever location is chosen in the header.
  3. A schedule open in the editor with the Add service form open (New schedule > Add service), Distance ticked so a meter row shows too.
custom_steps:
1. On an interval row open the operator and read its two choices.
  2. On the calendar row choose "At" and read how the value control changes; pick 15 Nov.
  3. On the calendar row choose "Every" and read the number and unit controls.
  4. Hover the "Every" operator and read its tooltip.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Each interval row offers the operator "Every" or "At".
  • On the calendar row "At" turns the value into a day-and-month picker (e.g. 15 Nov); it never offers a month on its own.
  • With "Every" the calendar row has a number and a unit (days or months), both picked from lists, not typed; months run 1 to 12.
  • On the design the operator's tooltip reads "every rebases on the last completion. at is a fixed point that never moves."

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780, story SV-10559 (S2, Add a routine service to a schedule), Chunk 1 MR (Confluence 886931488) as edited 5 October 2026, S2 (Triggers and intervals; S2-R6, S2-R7, S2-R8); Design board "Chunk 1.dc.html" (MR V2 Claude Design project, version of 6 October 2026), service form P04 to P06; read 6 Oct 2026. Source-verified 6 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-R6: “Each interval row has an operator, "Every" or "At". "Every" repeats and counts again from each completion. "At" is a fixed point”
  • S2-R7: “On the calendar row, choosing "At" turns the value into a (calendar) day-and-month picker, for example 15 Nov. "At" is never a month on its own”
  • S2-R8: “The calendar interval carries a number and a unit, days or months, both chosen from a list rather than typed. Months run 1 to 12 and days are whole numbers”
  • Design board, service form (operator tooltip): “every rebases on the last completion. at is a fixed point that never moves.”
